text: {"lessons":["I often sold Stocks B and C only when they were above my average cost, while delaying a sale of Stock D until a sizable loss; I should base each decision on future prospects and portfolio fit, not my purchase price or the pain of realizing a loss.","Selling winners brought satisfaction, but repeated partial sales are not a plan by themselves; I should set portfolio-level targets and rebalance deliberately rather than react to gains.","Buying more Stock D after it fell did not ensure a recovery, and selling it later at a loss did not undo the risk; I should avoid averaging down without a clear thesis and keep diversification and position sizes in view."]}
